finding.rootCause: the autonomy pump derives receipt.receivedAt from the current tick time; after a process dies after receipt persistence but before run-snapshot persistence, restart re-enters the same run/session/task/sequence at a later local time. The ledger previously compared receivedAt as semantic execution truth, turning this legitimate replay into autonomy-execution-receipt-conflict and preventing the snapshot from ever advancing.
finding.repair: receivedAt is now first-observation metadata excluded from semantic conflict comparison. The first persisted receivedAt remains immutable. Provider/worker/task/result-status truth remains conflict-sensitive.

hostileCasesProven: concurrent duplicate execution receipt creates one durable row
restart replay with later local receivedAt reuses the first durable receipt
same receipt identity with different worker truth fails closed
same receipt identity with different result status fails closed

newlyDiscoveredOpenRisk.finding: queue requeueDeadLetter currently accepts any non-empty reconciliationReceipt object for uncertain/reconcile work, while the server retry route does not expose a body for supplying a structured receipt. This should be hardened into a job/dead-letter-occurrence-bound SAFE_TO_RETRY evidence contract and wired through the operator route before runtime closure.
newlyDiscoveredOpenRisk.reasonNotPatchedInThisCommit: queue.mjs and server.mjs were only available through truncated source views in this execution surface; rewriting either from an incomplete view would risk source amputation.

truthBoundary: This receipt proves the focused receipt-ledger crash replay behavior under exact target/test bytes with reconstructed import contracts. It is not full-repository green, real-PostgreSQL proof, hosted exact-head verification, or external/commercial evidence.
